title: fix(spec): name the surface, list the keys and suggest the rename on the `protection` block's unknown-key refusal
body:
Fixes #16845

Clause-②: no — this PR puts no new key on any published payload and moves no accept set. Measured rather than asserted: an identical parse-probe script run against the built `dist` before and after (declared key set, two accepted inputs with their returned data, seven rejections with issue codes, one valid block through a real mount) `diff`s to exit 0 with sha256 `2d2e9b02…` on both sides; `check:authorable-surface` is green with **zero** regeneration and the generated artifacts are byte-unchanged; and a two-sided ablation (pre-fix declaration restored on disk, proved by blob hash) leaves the 15 accept-set pins unable to tell the two schemas apart while exactly the 5 refusal-text pins go red.

`ProtectionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`) was a bare `z.object({ … }).strict()` with **no error map**. Its closure was never the defect — the **message** was. Converted to the `strictObject` helper, mirroring the `PluginPermissionsSchema` conversion in #16328 / PR #16846.

---

## 1. Before / after, measured by running a parse

Both transcripts are from the **built `dist`**, the same channel the card's own evidence used (`dist/ai/index.mjs`, `dist/shared/index.mjs`), on this branch: `47863f4fb` for the before and `46e0e0b89` for the after. Reading the source cannot distinguish "has an error map" from "has an error map that says something useful", so both were produced by `safeParse`.

**BEFORE** — `AgentSchema.safeParse({ name: 'a', protection: { lockk: 'system' } })`

```
RAW  code=unrecognized_keys path=["protection"] keys=["lockk"]
RAW  message:
       Unrecognized key: "lockk"

FORMATTED (formatZodError):
  ✗ protection: Unrecognized key: "lockk"
```

**AFTER** — same input, same channel

```
RAW  code=unrecognized_keys path=["protection"] keys=["lockk"]
RAW  message:
       Unrecognized key(s) on the `protection` block of this metadata item: `lockk`.
       Did you mean `lockk` → `lock`? This block has refused unknown keys since it was
       introduced, but through zod's own bare message: a one-keystroke `lockk` was echoed
       back and nothing else — no surface, no declared-key list, no rename — while every
       neighbouring block on the same item named all three. It is mounted on very nearly
       every authorable metadata type in the platform (objects, views, dashboards,
       datasets, reports, apps, flows, webhooks, permissions, positions, email templates,
       agents, tools, skills), so that bare message was what an author saw wherever a
       protection key was misspelled. The declared keys are `lock`, `reason` and `docsUrl`.
```

All three parts an author needs are now present: the **surface**, the offending **key**, the **rename** — plus the declared-key list, which this template carries in `history`.

### A measured wrong answer, corrected

Two entries in the alias table are not decoration. Measured on the pre-fix build with the helper's own `findClosestMatches` against the declared keys and the real length-relative budget:

| authored | budget | pre-fix suggestion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `docs` | 2 | **`lock`** |
| `link` | 2 | **`lock`** |

`docs` and `link` are each two edits from `lock`, inside the budget for a four-character key, so the fallback pointed an author who meant the documentation URL at the lock policy. That is ledger finding 7's shape — this campaign's own fix signposting into a second rejection — and `docs`/`link` → `docsUrl` is why those two rows carry judgement rather than typing.

---

## 2. "Never enumerated" or "deliberately accepted"?

**Never enumerated, and by campaign design — not deliberately accepted.** No verdict was ever taken on this file. Two measurements, each with controls:

**Absence, with a lit and a dark control.** In `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md`:

| probe | reads | what it matched |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `shared/protection` (the claim) | **0** | — |
| `protection.zod.ts` (widened) | 1 | line 501, `kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts` — a **different file**, in a note about a counting bug |
| `kernel/manifest.zod.ts` (**lit control**) | 2 | the coarse `kernel/` row and its #14192 split |
| `shared/pr0tection.zod.ts` (**dark control**) | 0 | — |

And in the generated counts artifact, `docs/audits/…-ledger.counts.md`: `protection` reads **0**; the only `shared/` line in the whole file is `| `shared/` | 20 |`, under the heading **"Other directories (untriaged)"**.

**Why that silence carries no information — two independent reasons.**

1. **`shared/` is one of the nine untriaged directories.** The campaign gave per-file rows to exactly five directories (`ui/`, `data/`, `automation/`, `security/`, `studio/`); the other nine are "classified coarsely, per directory rather than per file". The ledger's own closing note says the untriaged nine "were never in the ruling's forced scope … a future campaign that wants them starts by giving them per-file rows, at which point this gate begins holding them too." So no row was ever owed here, and none was ever withheld.
2. **Even a per-file row would not have surfaced this.** The ledger's ratchet axis is `strip` → `strict`. `ProtectionSchema` has been `.strict()` since it was introduced, so it counts in the `strict` column and could never carry a remaining-strip row. **The ratchet's axis is CLOSURE; this defect was MESSAGE QUALITY on an already-closed shape.** A per-file row would have read "closed" and been correct.

**Does the ledger owe something? Yes — but an annotation, not a row.** The coarse `shared/` row's rationale read *"strictness decided at the consuming schema"*, and that is **false for this file**, measured: all **16** `protection: ProtectionSchema` mounts across **14** files are the bare `ProtectionSchema.optional()` — zero `.extend()`, `.merge()`, `.omit()` or re-posture among them (the only other `ProtectionSchema` reference in the tree is a type pin in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`). So both the strictness and the message are decided in `shared/` and inherited verbatim. A row is read as licence, which is the failure the `api/` and `kernel/` rows each already record; this is the third instance, annotated the same way and in the same table. ⛔ The row states explicitly that `shared/` remains **untriaged**, that this is **not** a per-file row, and that the population of *other* closed shapes still carrying zod's bare message is **NOT MEASURED** — #14722's rule that a sweep needs its own card with its own measured count is untouched.

The `check:strictness-ledger` gate is green over the annotation.

---

## 3. The surface-wording decision

`surface` is per-mount-context in every neighbouring adoption (*"the `permissions` block of this package manifest"*). This is **one declaring schema reached from 16 mount sites across 14 files** — verified at branch head, not taken from the card, which undercounts at four:

```
git grep -n "protection: ProtectionSchema" -- packages/spec/src | grep -v shared/protection.zod.ts
  → 16 lines, 14 files   (lit control: the declaring file itself reads 3 for `ProtectionSchema`;
                          dark control `protection: ProtektionSchema` reads 0)
```

Line numbers have moved since the card's comment measured them (`flow.zod.ts` 917→936, `object.zod.ts` 2374→2379, `app.zod.ts` 1556→1578, `dashboard.zod.ts` 982→1017), which is exactly why the mounts were located by text.

**Chosen: `'the `protection` block of this metadata item'`.** The alternative — transcribing the 16 mount contexts into the string — was rejected because it mints precisely the second copy of the truth `strictObject` exists to delete: the mount list moves (four of the 16 moved this week), and a stale copy here would be published as a confident sentence inside a rejection. Naming the **block** instead is true at every mount without naming one, it cannot drift as mounts come and go, and it matches what the author actually wrote and what the error path already shows them (`protection.lock`). The blast radius is carried where prose belongs, in `history`, hedged as *"very nearly every authorable metadata type"* so the illustrative list cannot become false.

The one transcription this file does keep — the declared-key list spelled into `history`, as the precedent does — is **pinned against the shape** rather than trusted (`the history key list is the shape's key list`), so it cannot drift.

---

## 4. Clause ② — **no**, and it is measured, not quoted

The card argues the change cannot move the accept set. I verified rather than repeated it.

**Parse-level probe, before and after, identical script against the built `dist`:** the declared key set, two accepted inputs with their returned data, seven rejections with their issue `code`s, and one valid block through a real mount.

```
diff before.B.txt after.B.txt   →  exit 0
sha256  2d2e9b0268251c03423fea88cc639ac5bd47d926182777ca37ad61b0c2889d2f  (both)
```

Byte-identical. Declared key set `["docsUrl","lock","reason"]` both sides; `unrecognized_keys` / `invalid_value` / `invalid_type` / `invalid_format` / `too_big` / `too_small` unchanged.

**Second, independent reading — the ablation.** With the pre-fix declaration restored on disk (blob `c99a8f94` → `8abc8306`, confirmed by hash and by the `strictObject(` anchor count going 1 → 0) and the **new tests unchanged**:

```
Tests  5 failed | 15 passed (20)
```

The five failures are exactly the five refusal-text pins — they can go red, so they measure something. The fifteen passes are every accept-set pin plus every pre-existing test: **the accept-set pins cannot tell the two schemas apart, which is clause ② from the other side.** Restore verified byte-exact afterwards (`git diff HEAD` = 0 bytes, on-disk blob `c99a8f94` = `HEAD` blob).

**Third:** `check:authorable-surface` is green with **zero** regeneration — the generated authorable-surface / JSON-schema artifacts are byte-unchanged, so the authored key set did not move.

⇒ the declaration line is at the top of this body. No `needs:contract-review` label applied.

---

## 5. Gates

**Green (exit 0, each captured before any pipe, landed to disk and read back):**

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — twice (before and after), via `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **471 files / 13260 tests passed**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — **all 15 generated artifacts up to date, nothing regenerated** (`check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:migration-registry`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:react-blocks`, `check:export-origins`, `check:declaration-map`, `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:liveness`, `check:test-typecheck`)
- spec source audits: `check:liveness` `check:empty-state` `check:exported-any` `check:dual-source-exports` `check:entry-nameability` `check:browser-reachable-entries` `check:llms-txt` `check:variant-docs` `check:yaml-examples` `check:duration-unit-keys` `check:objectui-pin-citations`
- root: `check:nul-bytes` `check:cross-package-test-inputs` `check:test-source-alias` `check:spec-parsed-alias` `check:doc-authoring` `check:merge-driver` `check:published-files` `check:type-check-coverage` `check:dts-closure` `check:undeclared-dep-imports` `check:keyed-text-bounds` `check:comment-mask-adoption` `check:comment-mask-corpus` `check:closing-keyword-parity` `check:reference-carrier-shape`
- changeset family: `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main`, `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:pm-changeset-deadline-census`
- docs: `docs-audit/check-affected-docs.mjs`, `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs`

**NOT MEASURED (declared, not skipped):**

- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — **exit 3**, the gate's own `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` state, not a finding: `--re-measure` refuses without the whole workspace build closure on disk ("nothing was measured, so this run says NOTHING about whether any DEBT or TEST_DEBT number is still correct"). Its coverage half, `check:type-check-coverage`, ran green. CI builds the closure before this step.
- `check:react-declaration-parity` — `EXTERNAL_INPUT_REQUIRED`; needs objectui's `sdui.manifest.json`, unproducible in this container.
- The whole-tree gate families and the five path-scheduled CI jobs (`Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`) — CI's own runs, declared to CI.

**Repo-wide lint, narrowed — and the narrowing is a measurement, three pieces of evidence:**

1. **Checked population, from eslint's own config, not a guess:** this repo runs one `eslint.config.mjs`, which *"never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file"* — the config's own words, at its line 328, recorded there with a positive control.
2. **File count, from `--format json`:** 2 files linted, **0 errors, 0 warnings**, `eslint --no-inline-config` exit 0.
3. **Invariance:** with no type-aware rule anywhere in the config, no verdict on an untouched file can depend on the contents of a file this diff changed. The narrowing therefore excludes nothing.

`pnpm lint` over the whole repo remains CI's run.

---

## 6. Acceptance notes (⛔ not filed — no carrier for either)

- **The population of *other* closed authorable shapes still carrying zod's bare message is NOT MEASURED.** The card deliberately declines the sweep and #14722's triage already ruled that one needs its own card with a measured population. Noted, not filed: no carrier — no open PR or queued card reaches that population, and filing an unmeasured sweep card is exactly what that ruling forbids.
- **The illustrative type list inside `history` can go stale** as metadata types are added or removed. It is hedged with *"very nearly every authorable metadata type in the platform"*, which stays true either way, and nothing gates the parenthetical. Noted deliberately; the load-bearing transcription in that sentence (the declared-key list) **is** pinned against the shape.

---

## 7. What is in the diff

| file | why |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts` | the conversion — the declaring schema only |
| `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.test.ts` | 5 refusal-text pins + 4 accept-set pins, all pre-existing tests kept |
| `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md` | the coarse `shared/` row annotated |
| `.changeset/protection-block-unknown-key-refusal.md` | `@objectstack/spec: patch` |

⛔ **The 16 mount sites are deliberately untouched** — this card edits the declaring schema, not its consumers, and the mounts inherit the new message with no edit.

⛔ Left **draft** deliberately: not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge armed.
